text:
Happy first Sunday back on standard time. It's a clear, sunny late morning with temperatures in the upper 40s, and the sun is doing its job. This afternoon climbs to a high near 57, a few degrees milder than yesterday felt. With sunset coming around 4:40 now, the best window for a walk or a ride is between noon and 3, before the light fades and it cools off quickly. A light jacket will do.

Tonight brings a few clouds and a low around 40, so it's not as cold as recent mornings. Monday looks mostly sunny and warmer, with a high near 62. A couple of the models push it into the mid 60s, and I'd lean toward the warmer side.

Tuesday is the one to watch. Clouds thicken, and a little light rain is possible late in the day, though it would be a sprinkle at most and not every model even has it. Wednesday is the real surprise, with highs in the upper 60s and maybe low 70s, and a gusty south breeze to go with it. The rain that matters arrives Thursday.

Cooler and mostly cloudy, high near 61, with on-and-off rain possible and a chilly 43 by night.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-11-01T11:25:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Temperatures becoming warmer heading into November.
  2. A cold front will move through the Northeast late this week bringing breezes and periods of rain possibly Thursday through the weekend.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 152 AM EST Sunday... Rainfall prospects for Tuesday are somewhat higher, and temperatures for Wednesday have been trended upwards to near record warmth in the St. Lawrence Valley.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Little in the manner of impactful weather is expected over the next several days. High pressure will move offshore, and that will allow warm air to gradually filter into the region under steady south to southwest flow. This will bring 50s today, and then 60s tomorrow. It'll still be on the dry side, but winds will generally be lighter where the lowest humidity values will be. Nighttime temperatures will also trend warmer, with only cooler hollows of sheltered valleys east of any mountain slopes below freezing tonight. There's still a tilted mid to upper level ridge that will be positioned to our west through about Tuesday. As it begins to translate eastwards, depending on the positioning of an upper vort, the surge of warm, moist advection could become collocated with marginal synoptic forcing. This would result in an area of clouds and light rain, mainly along the international border Tuesday into Tuesday night. Not every model scenario depicts rain, and so PoPs are mainly at or below 50 percent at this time. Once the upper ridge is offshore, temperatures will climb into the mid 60s to lower 70s for Wednesday in response to somewhat tighter pressure gradients as a surface low tracks over far northern Quebec Province. A few daily record highs may be in striking distance. Ushering in the warmth will be south winds gusting around 15-25 mph with localized observations around 30 mph, especially in the broader valleys. KEY MESSAGE 2: Model consensus favors a full meridional trough ejecting out of the Plains Wednesday night with a cold front passing through the Northeast between Thursday and Friday. Timing spread has narrowed a little, but model discrepancies remain on how fast the high pressure shifts eastward, the timing of the front itself, and the strength of frontal dynamics. Some models are stalling the boundary in the vicinity of Vermont streaming ample moisture across the region while others are more progressive with flow resulting in more distinct rounds of rainfall. While the details are sparse, most guidance agrees that there is a good shot at an extended period of rain chances with the trailing upper low becoming at least partially cut off. This would promote lingering shower chances through the weekend potentially into early next week. The details that are more predictable are continued warm temperatures under southerly flow Thursday with some southerly breezes ongoing as well. Beyond Thursday, temperatures are favored to cool back towards seasonal averages with coldest air locked well north of the region.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Hopefully you’ve remembered to turn your clocks back 1 hour, as we’re back to Standard Time. After a chilly but fair Halloween, today will be mostly sunny and pleasantly warmer with highs in the 50s to around 60 degrees...not a bad way to start November and the second half of fall. Monday will be dry and even warmer with highs in the mid-50s to low 60s. The week will continue to be dry before the chance for rain increases late in the week. Election Day may have an isolated shower north, otherwise it will be mostly cloudy with highs in the 50s, though a few low 60s are possible. The warmest day will be Wednesday with plenty of sunshine and highs in the 60s. A few spots may even hit 70 degrees. It will be breezy, so we’ll have to keep an eye on the fire danger. The risk is currently high in parts of the region, but it’s not expected to reach red flag status. We’ll keep an eye on it. A storm system will bring some needed rain late in the week and possibly into next weekend, though models differ with the track and duration. As of now, Thursday is expected to be mostly cloudy with showers likely. Friday and Saturday are a bit more uncertain, but the chance for showers may continue. High temperatures those days will be in the 50s with lows in the 40s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-01T14:38:00Z — same caveat): Sunny and warmer Sunday, as a south breeze develops — Sunday turns milder, with highs in the 50s to near 60, as a light south breeze develops. High pressure brings a mostly sunny sky through the day. A few more clouds arrive tonight, with the risk for a spot shower late. It won't be as cold, with lows in the 30s and 40s. Most of the upcoming workweek looks mild for early November, with highs in the 60s for several days. Monday will feature a blend of sun and clouds. The warmup continues, thanks to an active south breeze. Highs reach the mid-60s. Tuesday looks mostly cloudy with a period of light rain possible, especially during the afternoon and evening, as a warm front lifts through. Highs fall back to the upper 50s. Wednesday looks to be the warmest day, as highs reach the low to mid-70s for many towns! Expect a partly sunny sky. An area of low pressure brings the chance for widespread, beneficial rain late week. A few showers are possible Thursday, especially by afternoon, as highs stay in the 60s. Rain may be steady at times on Friday, with highs falling back to the upper 50s.
